Subject: Demo request — multiple regions, booking link showed wrong hour

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the quick note on the website — we'd like to schedule a demo for our payments team. We have folks in London (BST) and Sydney (AEST) who both need to join. I tried the Calendly link (https://calendly.com/redwood/demo) and selected "10:00" thinking it would show as 10:00 London time, but when the confirmation came through it was in Pacific time and the invite ended up as 02:00 for our Sydney folks.

I'm attaching a screenshot of the confirmation page. Can you: 1) confirm how the scheduling link determines the timezone; and 2) send a manual invite (ICS) that explicitly sets the timezone so we can add it to our calendars?

We can do a 14:00–15:00 BST / 23:00–00:00 AEST window most weekdays. If Calendly is unreliable I can accept a manual ICS.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>

Hi Elena —

Really sorry about the confusing behavior. Calendly will default the display to the visitor's browser locale or their Calendly account settings; we've seen cases where an embedded link or a corporate browser profile forces an en-US locale which flips the defaults to Pacific. That explains why your Sydney attendees saw an offset.

Two quick options so we get a time on everyone's calendars reliably:
- I can send a manual .ics for the exact slot with explicit TZ rules (I'll include both BST and AEST label).
- Or we can use a Chili Piper fallback redirect I keep for cross-region calls (https://redwood.app/fallback/chilipiper/demo-redirect) which forces the timezone via URL params.

If the BST/AEST window you suggested works, I'll draft an invite for 2028-09-06 14:00 BST / 23:00 AEST and include Marissa to run the demo. Marissa / Camila — can one of you confirm availability for that slot?

I'll also open a HubSpot ticket to track this (DEAL-8902) so the scheduling edge case is captured.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
